title: Make readiness and coverage gaps explainable
statement: As a delivery owner, author, or reviewer, I can see what each story still needs across Product, Design, Quality, and Implementation, why it is missing, and what safe action should happen next.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Requirements, prototype, UX, UI, technical-design, quality, implementation-trace, review-readiness, and completed-review states remain separate derived gates with concrete blockers.
Intentional section exclusions are revision-pinned, cited, and shown separately from covered and missing work; accepted delivery obligations cannot be silently excluded.
Work progress, a relation, a passing status, diff coverage, and reviewer approval cannot substitute for one another or for current immutable evidence.
The reviewer UI uses the stable Product, Design, Quality, and Implementation hierarchy and deep-links from criterion paths to prototypes, design Items, tests, and exact code.
Queries and UI projections are bound to one Saga and source snapshot and reject stale cursors rather than mixing revisions.
Completed review requires configured readiness gates plus current required report, prototype, slide, diagram, reference, and test-case decisions; it does not imply external merge authorization.
Each accepted criterion has separate Prototype, UX, UI, Technical, Quality, and Implementation states with concrete linked artifacts, exclusions, or gaps.
Each artifact counted toward a criterion also reports whether it reaches exact current diffs, keeping requirement-to-section and section-to-diff coverage distinct.
Machine-readable readiness orders safe next actions by blockers and dependencies without pretending sidebar order is execution order.
